description: This topic covers the parts, format, tone and language of informal (personal) and formal (official) letters, including how to write applications and simple official letters.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an informal letter?

options.text: A letter to your headmaster requesting a transfer
A letter to your cousin inviting her to your birthday party
A letter applying for a job at a bank
A letter of complaint to a shop manager

mcq.explanation: An informal letter is written to people we know well, such as relatives and friends, and a party invitation to a cousin fits this category.

mcq.questionText: How many addresses does a formal (official) letter usually contain?
mcq.explanation: A formal letter contains two addresses: the writer's address and the receiver's (recipient's) address.

mcq.questionText: Which salutation is most suitable for a formal letter when you do not know the receiver's name?
mcq.explanation: When the recipient's name is unknown, 'Dear Sir/Madam' is the polite and correct formal salutation.

mcq.questionText: An informal letter to a close friend would best begin with which salutation?
mcq.explanation: Informal letters use warm, personal greetings that name the friend, while the other options are formal or impersonal.

mcq.questionText: Which closing is correct for a formal letter that began with 'Dear Sir/Madam'?
mcq.explanation: When a formal letter starts with 'Dear Sir/Madam' (name unknown), it should close with 'Yours faithfully'.

mcq.questionText: Which closing is correct for a formal letter that began with the receiver's name, such as 'Dear Mr. Mwangi'?
mcq.explanation: When you know and use the recipient's name, the correct formal closing is 'Yours sincerely'.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of an application letter?

options.text: To share family news with a relative
To request a job, position, or place formally
To congratulate a friend on passing exams
To invite neighbours to a wedding

mcq.explanation: An application letter is a formal letter used to apply for something such as a job, school place, or position.

mcq.questionText: Where should the writer's address be placed in a letter?

options.text: At the bottom of the page after the signature
In the middle of the body
At the top, usually on the right side

mcq.explanation: The writer's own address is written at the top of the letter, traditionally on the right-hand side.

mcq.questionText: Which feature distinguishes the language of a formal letter from an informal one?

options.text: It uses slang and contractions freely
It uses polite, respectful and standard language
It uses emotional and chatty expressions

mcq.explanation: Formal letters require polite, respectful and standard English, avoiding slang, jokes and contractions.

mcq.questionText: What is the correct order of the main parts of a formal letter?

options.text: Addresses and date, salutation, subject, body, closing and signature

mcq.explanation: A formal letter follows the order of addresses and date, salutation, subject heading, body, then closing and signature.

mcq.questionText: In a formal letter, what does the 'subject' line tell the reader?

options.text: The main reason or topic of the letter
The date the letter was written

mcq.explanation: The subject line briefly states the main reason or topic so the reader knows the purpose at a glance.

mcq.questionText: Which of these would NOT normally appear in an informal letter?

options.text: A friendly opening asking about the reader's health
A warm closing like 'Your loving friend'

mcq.explanation: Informal letters do not include the receiver's address; only the writer's address and date appear at the top.

mcq.questionText: Below an official letter's closing, what should the writer add after their signature?
mcq.explanation: In an official letter the writer signs and then prints their full name clearly so the reader knows who wrote it.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence shows the polite tone expected in a formal request letter?

options.text: Give me the money right now.
I would be grateful if you could consider my request.
You must help me, no excuses!
Hey, sort this out for me, okay?

mcq.explanation: Formal letters use courteous expressions such as 'I would be grateful', showing respect and politeness.

mcq.questionText: Why is the date important in any letter?

options.text: It shows when the letter was written and helps keep records
It tells the reader the writer's age

mcq.explanation: The date records when the letter was written, which is useful for reference, filing and replying on time.

fib.questionText: A letter written to people we know well, such as friends and relatives, is called an _____ letter.
fib.explanation: Informal (or personal) letters are written to people we are close to and use a friendly tone.

fib.questionText: A letter written to organisations, offices or strangers for official purposes is called a _____ letter.
fib.explanation: Formal (official) letters are used for business and official communication and use polite, standard language.

fib.questionText: The greeting at the beginning of a letter, such as 'Dear Sir', is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The salutation is the opening greeting that addresses the reader.

fib.questionText: A formal letter that begins with 'Dear Sir/Madam' should end with 'Yours _____'.
fib.explanation: When the recipient's name is unknown, the correct closing is 'Yours faithfully'.

fib.questionText: A formal letter that uses the receiver's actual name should end with 'Yours _____'.
fib.explanation: When the recipient's name is used in the salutation, the correct closing is 'Yours sincerely'.

fib.questionText: A short heading that states the main reason of a formal letter is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The subject line summarises the purpose of the letter for the reader.

fib.questionText: The main part of the letter where the message is written is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The body contains the actual content and message of the letter.

fib.questionText: In a formal letter there are two addresses: the writer's address and the _____ address.
fib.explanation: A formal letter shows both the writer's address and the receiver's (recipient's) address.

fib.questionText: A formal letter written to ask for a job or a place is known as an _____ letter.
fib.explanation: An application letter formally requests a job, position or place.

fib.questionText: The writer's own address is usually written at the top _____ corner of the letter.
fib.explanation: Traditionally, the writer's address and date appear at the top right-hand corner.

tf.questionText: An informal letter includes the receiver's official address at the top.
tf.explanation: Only formal letters include the receiver's address; informal letters show just the writer's address and date.

tf.questionText: Slang and nicknames are acceptable in a formal letter.
tf.explanation: Formal letters require polite, standard language; slang and nicknames are not allowed.

tf.questionText: 'Yours faithfully' is used when a letter begins with 'Dear Sir/Madam'.
tf.explanation: When the recipient's name is unknown, the matching closing is 'Yours faithfully'.

tf.questionText: An application letter is a type of informal letter.
tf.explanation: An application letter is formal because it is written for an official purpose using polite language.

tf.questionText: Every letter, whether formal or informal, should include a date.
tf.explanation: The date is needed in all letters to show when they were written and for record keeping.

tf.questionText: An informal letter can use a warm closing such as 'Your loving friend'.
tf.explanation: Informal letters allow affectionate closings because they are written to people we know well.

tf.questionText: A subject line is a normal part of a personal letter to a friend.
tf.explanation: A subject line is a feature of formal letters, not personal informal ones.

tf.questionText: In a formal letter, the writer should sign and also print their full name clearly.
tf.explanation: Printing the full name after the signature helps the reader identify the writer in official letters.

tf.questionText: The tone of an informal letter is more relaxed and personal than that of a formal letter.
tf.explanation: Informal letters use a friendly, relaxed tone, while formal letters are polite and serious.

tf.questionText: The body of a formal letter should be long, chatty and full of personal feelings.
tf.explanation: The body of a formal letter should be clear, brief and to the point, not chatty or emotional.

summary.explanation: Letters are grouped by who they are written to and their purpose.

summary.questionText: Number of addresses in a formal letter
summary.correctAnswer: Two: the writer's and the receiver's addresses
summary.explanation: Formal letters need both addresses, while informal letters need only the writer's.
Used when the recipient's name is unknown.

summary.questionText: Closing when the receiver's name is used
summary.explanation: Used in formal letters where the name appears in the salutation.

summary.correctAnswer: To formally request a job, position or place
summary.explanation: It is a formal letter used for official requests.

summary.correctAnswer: Address(es), date, salutation, body, closing and signature
summary.explanation: Formal letters add a subject line and the receiver's address.

summary.correctAnswer: Polite, respectful and standard, with no slang

summary.explanation: It is written to people we know well.

summary.correctAnswer: It states the main reason or topic of the letter
summary.explanation: It appears in formal letters to guide the reader.

summary.correctAnswer: At the top, usually on the right side
summary.explanation: It appears before the date in both letter types.

hoq.questionText: Halima starts her letter with 'Dear Madam' and ends with 'Yours faithfully'. Which rule has she broken?

options.text: She used the wrong closing; since 'Dear Madam' shows respect but no name, 'Yours faithfully' is actually correct
She should have used 'Yours sincerely' because 'Dear Madam' identifies a specific person
She used the wrong closing because 'Dear Madam' uses no actual name, so 'Yours faithfully' is right and no rule is broken
She should have closed with 'Lots of love' to match the formal opening

hoq.explanation: Because 'Dear Madam' does not give a real name, 'Yours faithfully' is the matching closing, so Halima has not broken any rule.

hoq.questionText: A student writes to a company: 'Hey, I really wanna work for you guys, hit me up!' Why is this opening unsuitable for an application letter?

options.text: It is too long and detailed
It uses slang and an over-casual tone instead of polite, formal language

hoq.explanation: An application letter is formal, so words like 'hey', 'wanna', 'guys' and 'hit me up' are inappropriate; polite standard English is required.

hoq.questionText: Juma puts the receiver's address, a subject line, and 'Yours sincerely' in a letter to his grandmother sharing holiday news. What is the best correction?

options.text: Keep everything because all letters need a receiver's address and subject line
Remove the receiver's address and subject line and use a warm closing, since this is an informal letter
Add a second subject line to make it clearer

hoq.explanation: A personal letter to a grandmother is informal, so the receiver's address and subject line are unnecessary and the closing should be warm, such as 'Your loving grandson'.
